scope: Rendered readability, visual decoding, spatial hierarchy, and consistency with the supplied captions. Numerical correctness, exact export dimensions, fonts, and interval construction are outside this review and remain for the separate auditor.

files_actually_inspected.method: Opened original PNG and inspected a resized final-size screen proxy.

screen_proxy.interpretation: These are final-size screen proxies, not calibrated print samples. The one-pixel PDF raster rounding difference does not change the visual comparison. Exact physical export dimensions and font sizes were not validated.

shared_observations: Both panels show the same seven readable labels in the same visible order; matching source-table first appearance was not independently checked.
Blue and orange/vermillion marks are distinguishable. The hollow and filled states remain distinguishable at the screen proxy, and no visible contradiction with the dashed reference line was found.

The batch offsets separate paired intervals without overlapping their lines. The empty batch positions for Background suppression, Temperature sensitivity, and Storage response agree visually with the supplied captions.
The reference at 1, the labeled ticks, and the axis label are visible in both panels. Neither panel contains a title, subtitle, or prose footnote.
Both captions explicitly identify synthetic data, unknown independent sample size and interval method, pre-supplied intervals, and the absence of a significance claim.
The PNG and 96 dpi PDF views of each arm show the same apparent layout and decoding. This is visual consistency only, not an export audit.

A.mark_visibility: All marks and lines can be read at the proxy, but thin interval strokes and the compressed horizontal data span make endpoints and small relative differences less immediate than in B.
A.interval_separation: Generous vertical separation and single-line labels give straightforward row lookup. Approximate visible axis width is 167 px in the 529 px proxy.
A.ticks_and_labels: Single-line readout labels and tick labels are legible. The axis label does not name the log scale, which the separate caption explains.
A.legend: Batch and fill-state keys are visibly separated, making their independent roles easy to understand. The fill-state legend extends farther horizontally than the data region.
A.whitespace_and_hierarchy: A large white region to the right of the narrow data axis remains unused below the legend. The legend competes with the data region in horizontal extent.

B.mark_visibility: Longer interval spans, visible end caps, and stronger strokes make interval endpoints and reference overlap easier to read at the proxy.
B.interval_separation: Paired intervals remain clearly separated. Approximate visible axis width is 384 px in the 529 px proxy.
B.ticks_and_labels: Readout labels mostly wrap to two lines and remain legible without collisions. The axis label explicitly states log scale; light vertical guides help position lookup while remaining below the marks in visual emphasis.
B.legend: The compact two-column legend leaves the data region visually primary. Row alignment puts Batch A beside Includes 1 and Batch B beside Excludes 1, so the independence of the two encodings could be stated more clearly through grouping or spacing.
B.whitespace_and_hierarchy: The plotted data uses most of the available horizontal width. The space between category groups is sufficient, with no visible clipping or crowding.

findings.location: Data axis and right-side legend area
findings.evidence: At the final-size proxy, the data axis is approximately 167 px wide while the fill-state legend spans about 200 px, and a broad right-side blank area persists below the legend. The shortest intervals therefore occupy relatively few screen pixels.
findings.requirement: Keep the data visually primary and support easy endpoint and reference-overlap reading at the intended proportions.
findings.action: If revising, allocate more canvas width to the data axis and arrange the legend compactly; retain the agreed font size.

findings.evidence: The first row aligns Batch A with Interval includes 1 and the second aligns Batch B with Interval excludes 1. The two independent legend columns are understandable, but the row alignment can suggest an association during a quick glance.
findings.requirement: Decode batch color and interval fill state as independent visual channels.
findings.action: If revising, increase the separation between the legend groups or give each group a compact heading without enlarging the legend footprint.

findings.evidence: The caption begins with Figure 1; no assigned figure number was supplied for this blind comparison.
findings.requirement: Figure numbering should follow the known manuscript context.
findings.action: Confirm the manuscript figure number, or omit it until assigned. This does not affect plot decoding.

external_checks.reason: A separate independent auditor owns these checks; this review did not inspect source data, source scripts, font metadata, or SVG internals.

comparison.condition: Assuming the separate numerical and export audit confirms both panels meet the required data and export specifications.
comparison.rationale: B gives the horizontal interval comparison substantially more space, makes endpoints and the relationship to 1 easier to inspect, and keeps the legend compact relative to the data. A has the advantage of unwrapped labels and clearer separation of the two legend roles, but its unused right-side space and narrow plotting span impose a larger reading cost.
comparison.subjective_confidence: Moderately high for this screen-proxy visual comparison; it is not a quantitative quality score or a print-validation claim.

residual_notes: No blocking rendered readability or caption-meaning issue was observed in either arm.
Available vector metadata was later reported to contain program-identifying information. It was not inspected, and this disclosure occurred only after the initial preference and reports were saved.
This review cannot certify calibrated print legibility, numerical correctness, exact fonts, or physical export dimensions.
Both arms retain minor presentation notes. The preference does not establish journal acceptance or broader performance across other figures.
status_scope: Rendered visual readability and supplied-caption consistency only, pending the separate numerical/export audit.
